territorial_scope.description: Applies to covered integrated circuit products exported, reexported or in-country transferred from the United States to or in foreign countries.

evidence.quote: before it is exported, reexported, or in-country transferred to or in a foreign country

summary.short: As introduced, H.R. 3447 would require the Secretary of Commerce to make covered integrated circuit products carry chip security mechanisms such as location verification before export, reexport or in-country transfer, and would require licensees to report diversion or tampering.
summary.long: The bill, titled the Chip Security Act, directs the Secretary of Commerce to require covered integrated circuit products (ECCN 3A090, 3A001.z, 4A090, 4A003.z and successors) to carry chip security mechanisms implementing location verification before export, reexport or in-country transfer to a foreign country, not later than 180 days after enactment. Licensees must promptly report credible information of unauthorized location, diversion or tampering to the Under Secretary of Industry and Security. Within one year the Secretary must assess additional mechanisms and report to the appropriate congressional committees; any secondary mechanisms must then be required within two years of that assessment, prioritizing confidentiality. The Secretary may verify ownership and location of exported products and keep a record of their location and end-user. Starting two years after enactment and annually for three years, the Secretary must assess new mechanisms and report, including on export-control flexibility. Section 2 findings are not operative. The bill sets no penalties of its own.

relations.target_text: Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (50 U.S.C. 4801 et seq.)
relations.note: Cited for the definitions of export, in-country transfer and reexport (Sec. 3(4)-(6)), for licences granted under the Act (Sec. 4(a)(2), Sec. 4(c)(3)), and as a purpose of the assessment (Sec. 4(b)(1)(A)(i)(I)). The text does not state that this Act is made under that Act.

evidence.quote: section 1742(3) of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (50 U.S.C. 4801(3))

notes: Introduced bill ('A BILL'); the text has no enactment or other event dates, so all deadlines are relative to enactment. Only one external instrument is referenced (the Export Control Reform Act of 2018); the Export Control Classification Numbers are cited without naming the regulation that sets them, and 'Under Secretary of Industry and Security' is used without definition. Internal inconsistency: Sec. 4(b)(2)(B) says 'The report required by paragraph (1)', but the report is required by Sec. 4(b)(2)(A), while paragraph (1) is the assessment. Sec. 2 (sense of Congress) is non-operative.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment was found. The numbers in the text are procedural time limits (180 days, one year, two years, three years), which are coded as events, not thresholds. Covered products are defined by Export Control Classification Number (3A090, 3A001.z, 4A090, 4A003.z) and successor classifications, which are product classifications rather than numeric cutoffs.
